overview: Türkiye, also known as Turkey, lies mostly in Western Asia, with a small part in south-eastern Europe. Its capital is Ankara, but its largest city is Istanbul, which sits on both sides of the Bosphorus strait. Modern Türkiye was founded in 1923 by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, after the fall of the Ottoman Empire, which had ruled much of the region for more than 600 years.

geography.text: Most of Türkiye is the Anatolian peninsula, a high central plateau ringed by mountains. It has coasts on four seas: the Black Sea, the Mediterranean, the Aegean and the Sea of Marmara. In the east are high mountains, including Mount Ararat, the country's highest peak, and the sources of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Earthquakes are common.

history.text: Anatolia was home to some of the world's earliest settlements and to empires such as the Hittites and the Byzantines. In 1453 the Ottomans captured Constantinople, now Istanbul, and their empire ruled much of south-eastern Europe, the Middle East and North Africa for centuries. After its defeat in the First World War, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk founded the modern Republic of Türkiye in 1923.

events.title: Çatalhöyük
events.text: One of the world's earliest large settlements grows on the Anatolian plain.

events.title: Constantinople captured
events.text: Sultan Mehmed II takes the Byzantine capital.

events.title: Siege of Vienna
events.text: The Ottoman advance into Europe is halted at Vienna.

events.title: Republic
events.text: Atatürk founds the Republic of Türkiye.

events.title: Earthquakes
events.text: Two huge earthquakes kill more than 50,000 people in Türkiye and Syria.

government.text: Türkiye is a presidential republic. A 2017 referendum gave the President wide powers and abolished the post of Prime Minister. Recep Tayyip Erdoğan has led the country since 2003, first as Prime Minister and then as President. The Grand National Assembly is elected every five years. Türkiye is a NATO member.

economy.text: Türkiye has a large and varied economy. It makes cars, clothing, steel and appliances, and is a major farm producer of hazelnuts, figs and apricots. Tourism is huge. In recent years it has faced very high inflation.

culture.text: Türkiye bridges Europe and Asia, with Istanbul spread across both continents. Its heritage includes Byzantine and Ottoman architecture such as Hagia Sophia, as well as Turkish coffee, carpets, kebabs and baklava. The Whirling Dervishes perform a dance of Sufi meditation.

items.title: Hagia Sophia
items.text: Built as a church in 537, later a mosque, then a museum, then a mosque again.

items.title: Cappadocia
items.text: Fairy chimney rock formations and hot-air balloons.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Türkiye finished third at the 2002 World Cup. Oil wrestling at Kırkpınar, held since 1346, is one of the oldest sporting events in the world. Türkiye's women's volleyball team is among the best in the world.

items.text: Third place at the men's World Cup.
